text:
A: Alright! Liam. How you doing?
B: Hiya, I'm Gemma. Oh, you've got the decks! I said that about your photo, you look ever so friendly.
A: Cheers, Gemma. Teacher, yeah? I can always tell.
B: Ha, everyone's said that today. Head of Maths, a secondary in Nottingham. I'm in Beeston.
A: Maths. I were rubbish at maths. Then I sell cars and it's all percentages, finance, APR, so joke's on me.
B: That's what I tell my lot! You need it in every job. What do you sell?
A: New and used, dealership in Warrington. And I sort the finance.
B: Oh, I hate buying cars. My husband does all of that, I just sit there feeling like I'm being had.
A: You probably are, to be fair. Nah, I'm joking. I'm honest, me. Mostly.
B: Mostly! I'll remember that.
A: Did you go to uni for the maths, then?
B: Nottingham Trent, then my PGCE. I was the first in my family to go, actually. My dad was a fitter, my mum was a dinner lady.
A: That's brilliant, that. Proper. I started a degree, Music Journalism at Salford. Stopped going in second year. I were meant to be writing an essay on Joy Division and I went to Ibiza instead.
B: Oh, Liam! What did your mum say?
A: She didn't speak to me for about a week. Then she just said, well, get a job then. So I did. Best thing that happened, probably. Probably.
B: You sort of said that twice, there.
A: Ha, did I? Ah, you know. You wonder sometimes. Anyway. What's your fella do?
B: Rob's an electrician, self-employed. He'd get on with that other Liam, the Forest one. They'd talk about EV chargers for hours.
A: Oh, we did! We're going to do a deal, me and him. Every customer wants a charger now.
B: Rob says the same. Do you have kids?
A: Not yet. Me and Jess have been together six years. She keeps bringing it up.
B: And you keep changing the subject?
A: How'd you know that?
B: I've got a fifteen-year-old, I know when someone's changing the subject! No, I'm only teasing, sorry. Don't mind me.
A: Nah, you're right, though. It's not that I don't want it. I just don't see the rush, do you know what I mean? What about you, how old are yours?
B: Maisie's fifteen, Josh is twelve. He only eats beige food. Chicken nuggets, chips, cob, nothing green.
A: A cob! I've heard about this cob. Barm, Gemma. It's a barm.
B: Oh, don't you start, I've had...
